# local 0004: mcs51: compiler crash for __reentrant functions that return a struct and have a non-struct first parameter

- Category: [Problems without a ticket](../../unreported.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17158
- Recommended action: Make the front end and aopArg agree on register parameters of __reentrant functions that return a struct.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The compiler crashes with a segmentation fault in `genReceive` in `src/mcs51/gen.c` for the file
below. It was compiled with `sdcc -mmcs51 -c r1.c` on r17158.

```c
struct s { unsigned char a; int b; unsigned char c; };

struct s r1 (unsigned char x) __reentrant
{
  struct s r;
  r.a = x;
  r.b = 1;
  r.c = 2;
  return r;
}
```

The function compiles without `__reentrant`, and it compiles without the keyword under
`--stack-auto` as well. A `__reentrant` function with the parameter list `(void)` compiles too.

## Cause

The iCode of `r1` has a `RECEIVE` for `x`, which means that the front end has marked `x` as a
register parameter. `genReceive` asks `aopArg` for the registers of the parameter. `aopArg`
returns 0 for every parameter of functions that return a struct, because the registers stay free
for the hidden pointer to the result. `genReceive` dereferences the result without a check.

The source gives an origin for the mark. This part was read and not tested. In `src/SDCC.y` the
rule `declarator2_function_attributes` appends the attribute to the declarator with `addDecl`, and
`addDecl` calls `processFunc` in `src/SDCCsymt.c`. The return type is not in the function type at
that time, so `_mcs51_regparm` in `src/mcs51/main.c` finds no struct and accepts the first
parameter. `processFunc` runs again when the return type is known, and that run does not clear
`SPEC_REGPARM`.

## Related

The defect was found with test cases for bug #3847, which concerns struct values that functions
return from a call.
